minor.issue: Does not say the control group did volume- and intensity-matched circuit training, so the comparator is unclear.
No effect sizes or pre/post values. It also omits that only 5 m, agility, deficit, AH and AG differed between groups after training (30 m and AQ did not).
Suggests using the circuit in late reconditioning, which the study did not test.

critical.claim: "although this was a single-group, single-team study"
critical.source_says: "They were randomly divided into two 16-person control and experimental groups."

minor.issue: Assigns the speed (2x/wk) and agility (3x/wk) sessions to the experimental group only. The source says only the targeted strength training was experimental-only, so whether controls also did speed/agility is ambiguous.
Does not note that AQ did not differ between groups after training.

note: B is more precise and quantitatively correct (pre/post values, matched-circuit control, the no-injury caveat), but its athleteDev wrongly calls the randomised two-group trial a single-group study and needs a one-phrase fix. A is accurate but thinner.
